description: Rules that no record can decide. Each entry states why; the list is the honest boundary of what this suite verifies (CON-24, CON-25).

rules.CORE-4: Obligation on a producer's expectations: a record cannot express that its author must not rely on unknown members surviving a round trip.
rules.CORE-11: Extensions must not redefine core semantics. Redefinition is a question of intent; no structural check distinguishes an extension from a restatement.
rules.CORE-12: File-layout convention: where a record sits relative to its artifact is a storage decision, not a property of the record's content.
rules.CORE-13: File-naming convention for directories holding several artifacts; it constrains names on disk, which the suite does not inspect.
rules.CORE-14: A recommended media type for transport. It is a property of the channel, not of the record.
rules.CORE-15: A record must not be embedded in its artifact. A file containing its own digest would have to be a fixed point of SHA-256; the rule forbids a construction that cannot exist for a conformant record.
rules.ID-6: The name is informational and must never be used as an identifier: an obligation on consumers, which no record can demonstrate.
rules.ID-9: One artifact per record is structural: a record carrying several artifacts cannot satisfy ID-1, so there is no second shape to test.
rules.ID-13: Different bytes must have different identifiers. This follows necessarily from ID-8, which derives the identifier from the digest; a record cannot violate ID-13 while satisfying ID-8.
rules.ID-14: Consumers must not infer work-level identity from section 01. That is a prohibition on consumer behaviour, not a property of the record.
rules.ID-15: Awareness of byte-representation instability is an obligation on the producer's understanding, invisible in any file.
rules.SCH-5: Variorum defines no ordering at all, so there is no implementation surface that could compare labels across schemes and fail.
rules.SCH-6: A delegation statement: ordering belongs to the scheme's authority. It constrains documentation, not records.
rules.SCH-9: A strictly increasing sequence across a lineage is an obligation spanning several records of one work; the suite decides one record at a time and carries no work resolver.
rules.LIN-9: A consumer must still use the artifact when a parent record is missing. Consumer behaviour, not a record property.
rules.LIN-10: Work-level identity requires resolving a path through several records; testing it would test a graph algorithm rather than the format.
rules.LIN-11: Whether a fork starts a new work is decided when the graph is resolved, not when one record is read.
rules.LIN-12: Whether generation extends or splits a work is a semantic judgement about the parent edge, outside any single record.
rules.LIN-13: Advice about how much ancestry a producer chooses to store. Both choices yield valid records.
rules.REC-13: The prohibition on claiming 'full' determinism without verifying it depends on a re-execution that no record contains.
rules.REC-17: A preference between two valid ways of referencing an input. Both the id form and the URI form conform (REC-15).
rules.REC-20: A statement about how a recipe must be read, not about what a recipe contains.
rules.REC-21: Consumers must not report reproducibility from a recipe alone. Consumer behaviour.
rules.STA-13: Superseded artifacts must remain retrievable. A retention obligation on storage; a record cannot demonstrate that its bytes survive.
rules.STA-14: State must not encode quality or preference. No structural test can separate a decision from a judgement about the same artifact.
rules.ATT-8: Signature verification needs key material that the format deliberately does not distribute.
rules.ATT-9: Independent verification of several signatures requires the same key material as ATT-8.
rules.ATT-10: Consumers must not infer endorsement between signers. Consumer behaviour.
rules.ATT-11: A statement about what a signature does not establish. Semantics, not structure.
rules.ATT-12: Consumers must state what was verified. Consumer behaviour.
rules.SEM-6: An ordering obligation on consumers: no record decides how records are compared, and equal precedence between two versions is not a property of either one alone.
rules.C2P-7: A consumer obligation: reporting a contradiction between a manifest's ingredients and a record's lineage requires both documents and a judgement about which pair of artifacts they describe.
rules.C2P-8: A consumer obligation about signature scope: no record decides what a reader infers from a valid C2PA signature, and neither signature covers the other document.
rules.SWH-7: A consumer obligation that needs the artifact's bytes: the record validator never sees them, so it cannot recompute a content's SWHID or detect a claim that disagrees with the file.
rules.SWH-8: A consumer obligation about what an identifier covers: no record can demonstrate that a reader refrained from treating a tree, commit, tag or snapshot identifier as the artifact's bytes.
rules.SPDX-7: A consumer obligation that needs three things the record does not carry: the artifact's bytes, the SPDX document the claim names, and a resolver for both. The comparison of a file element's SHA256 checksum with the digest happens outside any record.
rules.SPDX-8: A consumer obligation about the conclusions a bill of materials licenses: that a verification code covers a set rather than a file, and that a claim without 'element' names nothing, are both facts about what a reader may infer, not properties of a record.
